# ASML Reports Strong Q1 2026 Results and Raises Annual Outlook

_[According to a report](https://www.indexbox.io/store/branch/semiconductors/) from Yahoo Finance, semiconductor equipment manufacturer [ASML Holding](https://app.indexbox.io/companies/profile/4770682/) ( [NASDAQ: ASML](https://www.indexbox.io/store/netherlands/)) recently disclosed its financial results for the first quarter of 2026. The company achieved net sales of 8.8 billion euros, with gross margins reaching 53%. Net income was reported at 2.8 billion euros, resulting in a net profit margin of 31.8%._

Based on this performance, ASML increased its full-year guidance. The company now anticipates net sales for the year to be between 36 billion and 40 billion euros, with gross margins projected in the range of 51% to 53%. The midpoint of the sales guidance suggests a year-over-year growth rate around 16.2%.

## Market Position and Product Demand

ASML's lithography systems are considered a critical component in the construction of artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company holds a dominant position in the market for extreme ultraviolet, or EUV, machines. These systems are used by major chip manufacturers to produce advanced logic and memory semiconductors.

Company leadership indicated that memory customers have reported being sold out for the current year, with supply constraints expected to persist. For advanced logic chips, customers are reportedly building capacity for multiple production nodes while also increasing output for 2-nanometer designs to meet demand for AI-related products. Both memory and logic customers are increasing their capital expenditure plans for 2026 and later, backed by long-term commitments to ASML.

## Production and System Sales

Despite strong demand, ASML remains in the early stages of mass-producing its most advanced EUV systems, known as high-numerical-aperture models. The company sold only two of these High-NA systems during the first quarter. For the full year 2026, ASML forecasts production of 60 units of its Low-NA EUV systems.

In the first quarter, EUV systems accounted for 46.6% of the total net sales. Non-EUV systems represented 23.9% of sales, while service revenue from the existing installed base contributed 28.4%. The company noted that its current financial performance is primarily driven by its Low-NA EUV technology.

## Stock Performance and Market Context

ASML's share price has increased significantly over the past year, outperforming major technology indices. At the time of the report, the stock was trading at $1,410 per share. Reaching a $2,000 share price would require an approximate 42% gain from that level. Achieving a $1 trillion market capitalization, which would make it the first European company to do so, would require an 81% increase in share price.

This report provides a comprehensive view of the particle accelerator industry in the Netherlands, tracking demand, supply, and trade flows across the national value chain. It explains how demand across key channels and end-use segments shapes consumption patterns, while also mapping the role of input availability, production efficiency, and regulatory standards on supply.

Beyond headline metrics, the study benchmarks prices, margins, and trade routes so you can see where value is created and how it moves between domestic suppliers and international partners. The analysis is designed to support strategic planning, market entry, portfolio prioritization, and risk management in the particle accelerator landscape in the Netherlands.

By [Daniel Foelber](https://www.fool.com/author/20117/)–Apr 21, 2026 at 11:15AM EST

## Key Points

- The semiconductor lithography specialist beat earnings estimates and updated its guidance.

- Demand for logic and memory chips gives ASML a multi-year runway for accelerated growth.

- However, be aware that the stock’s valuation has gone from pricey to downright expensive.


Shares of semiconductor lithography specialist **ASML Holding**( [ASML](https://www.fool.com/quote/nasdaq/asml/) +2.81%) have more than doubled over the last year -- crushing the performance of the broader tech sector and **Nasdaq Composite**. At $1,410 per share at the time of this writing, ASML would need to gain around 42% to surpass $2,000 per share, and 81% to become the first European company to surpass [$1 trillion in market capitalization](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/03/20/what-if-asml-trillion-dollar-stock/).

Here's why ASML's investment thesis is stronger than ever, and what could hold the [tech stock](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/) back from surpassing $2,000 per share.

![Lazers hitting a silicon wafer.](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Feditorial%2Fimages%2F866114%2Flazers-hitting-a-silicon-wafer.jpg&w=3840&op=resize)

Image source: Getty Images.

## ASML's blowout results

ASML reported its first-quarter 2026 earnings on April 15, and the results couldn't have been much better. ASML delivered 8.8 billion euros in net sales, 53% gross margins, and 2.8 billion euros in net income for a net profit margin of 31.8%. It also raised its full-year guidance to 36 billion-40 billion euros in net sales and gross margins between 51% and 53% -- representing year-over-year sales growth around 16.2% at the midpoint.

The company's lithography systems play an integral role in artificial intelligence (AI) [infrastructure investment](https://www.fool.com/research/ai-energy-use/). Lithography is arguably the most complex and important step in the fabrication of AI chips. And ASML has a virtual monopoly on extreme ultraviolet (EUV) machines, which allows manufacturers like **Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing**, **Samsung Electronics**, and **Intel** to support [next-generation designs of highly advanced chips](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/04/12/generational-buying-opportunity-broadcom-stock/), like those made by **Nvidia**, **Broadcom**, **Advanced Micro Devices**, and **Micron Technology**.

ASML continues to see increased demand for advanced logic chips and memory. ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet said the following on the first-quarter 2026 earnings call:

> So if we look at memory, what our customers tell us is that they are sold out for 2026. And their supply constraints will last beyond 2026. For advanced logic, we see our customers building capacity for several nodes, while they also continue to ramp 2 nm in order to address the AI products.

ASML said that memory and logic customers are ramping up their capital expenditures for 2026 and beyond, supported by long-term customer commitments. However, ASML is still early in mass-producing its EUV systems, especially its most advanced high-numerical-aperture (High NA) versions. In Q1, ASML sold just 2 High-NA EUV systems.

For 2026, ASML is forecasting production of 60 Low-NA EUV systems. In fact, Low-NA EUV is driving the bulk of ASML's current performance. In Q1, ASML had 8.8 billion euros in net sales, of which 46.6% were EUV systems, 23.9% was non-EUV systems, and 28.4% was servicing its existing installed base.

## ASML is an innovation machine

The [long-term bull case on ASML](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/03/20/what-if-asml-trillion-dollar-stock/) centers on the fact that the company is still relatively early into high-volume production and delivery of High-NA EUV systems. And given that next-generation fabs will need these machines to [produce cutting-edge chips](https://www.fool.com/research/data-center-revenue-ai-companies/), ASML effectively has a multiyear runway for steady, high-margin growth.

Management outlined this roadmap in its Q1 2026 earnings presentation through high-volume manufacturing of its existing High-NA EUV systems, as well as more advanced systems in development extending out to 2033 to handle even more advanced logic and memory manufacturing processes.

ASML's business model is perfectly built to fund multibillion-dollar research and development efforts. Sales from servicing its installed base alone were more than double its research and development costs in its latest quarter.

## Returning capital to shareholders

Despite record R&D spending, ASML's overall earnings growth leaves plenty of cash leftover to return to shareholders. In its Q1 earnings release, ASML announced a planned 17% increase in its dividend. It bought back 7.6 billion euros in stock from 2022 to 2025, including a whopping 1.7 billion euros in the fourth quarter of 2025. ASML is accelerating its buybacks, with a new 12 billion euro program from 2026 through 2028. Already, it executed 1.1 billion euros in buybacks in Q1 2026.

Buying back stock helps reduce the share count and more than offset stock-based compensation -- making ASML a better value for long-term investors. And although ASML isn't a high-yield stock by any means, the growing dividend is an added benefit for long-term investors seeking passive income without selling shares.

## ASML remains a buy for long-term investors

ASML is a foundational AI stock to build a portfolio around. Management just outlined why near-term demand continues to outpace supply, and why ASML is incredibly well positioned to lead lithography innovation over the long term. The company continues to operate with high margins and grow sales and earnings at an excellent pace.

The only downside to buying ASML now is its valuation. Since ASML's stock price has been rising much faster than earnings, its [valuation has become significantly more expensive](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/03/24/asml-buy-growth-tech-ai-stock/). ASML now sports a 39.3 forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio compared to a 10-year median P/E of 36. Meaning that even if ASML meets earnings expectations over the next year and the stock price goes nowhere, it will still trade at a premium to its historical average.

Therefore, investors buying ASML should only do so if they have at least a three- to five-year investment time horizon, as the stock could remain under a lot of near-term pressure as investors are already pricing in excellent results. But if ASML keeps delivering, it wouldn't be at all surprising if it blows past $2,000 per share in the coming years.

Chip equipment maker ASML ([ASML](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ASML?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "ASML Holding N.V.")) raised its full-year sales forecast, driven by AI infrastructure investments fueling semiconductor production that has boosted demand for its chipmaking machines.

Shares of ASML fell about 4% on Wednesday.

## Key Metrics

ASML — which makes extreme ultraviolet lithography, or EUV, and Deep Ultraviolet, or DUV, lithography system — saw first-quarter net sales increase about 13.3% year-over-year to €8.77B, [beating](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4575042-asml-beats-top-line-and-bottom-line-estimates-introduces-q2-and-updates-fy26-outlook?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "beating") estimates.

"The semiconductor industry's growth outlook continues to solidify, driven by ongoing AI-related infrastructure investments. Demand for chips is outpacing supply. In response, our customers are accelerating their capacity expansion plans for 2026 and beyond, supported by long-term agreements with their customers. In the past months, our customers have increased their expected short- and medium-term demand for our products. ASML's order intake continues to be very strong as a result, and we are closely aligned with our customers to support their demand in a combination of delivery of new systems and performance upgrades of their installed base," [said](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20473340-asml-reports-8_8-billion-total-net-sales-and-2_8-billion-net-income-in-q1-2026?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1#hasComeFromMpArticle "said") ASML's CEO Christophe Fouquet.

ASML noted last year that it would stop [reporting](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4399873-asml-surges-as-q4-bookings-soar-on-ai-demand-china-sales-to-see-normal-ratio-in-2025?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "reporting") order bookings after 2025, a key indicator of customer demand. The company said then that on an annual basis it will provide the total backlog.

Addressing ASML's ability to keep up with demand, CFO Roger Dassen said the company should be able to ship at least 60 systems for Low NA EUV in 2026. Dassen added that the company can get to at least 80 Low NA EUV units in 2027.

Fouquet noted that there is a lot of demand for advanced Memory and advanced Logic driven by investments in AI infrastructure. "We expect in fact that the supply will not meet the demand for the foreseeable future. So, this is creating a strong constraint in the end markets from AI to mobile and PC," said Fouquet. He added that "if we look at Memory, what our customers tell us is that they are sold out for 2026. And their supply constraints will last beyond 2026. For advanced Logic, we see our customers building capacity for several nodes, while they also continue to ramp 2 nm in order to address the AI products.

ASML's customers include leading chip manufacturers, such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( [TSM](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TSM?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited")) and Intel ( [INTC](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/INTC?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "Intel Corporation")).

## China Sales

China accounted for 19% of the total net system sales of about €6.3B in the first quarter of 2026. South Korea led with a 45% share, followed by Taiwan at 23%. The U.S. accounted for 12% of the total net system sales. In the fourth quarter of 2025, China accounted for 36% of the total net system sales of about €7.58B, followed by South Korea.

## Outlook

"These business dynamics underpin our expectation that 2026 will be another growth year for all our businesses," said Fouquet.

Fouquet noted that the company sees its Memory and Logic customers increasing their capital expenditure and trying to accelerate their capacity ramp in 2026 and beyond. "So this translates basically into higher lithointensity and a higher litho demand for ASML. So we're going to continue to work very closely with our customers to increase our capacity. We are doing that in 2026. We will continue to do that in 2027," Fouquet added.

For the second quarter of 2026, ASML expects total net sales to be between €8.4B and €9B with a gross margin between 51% and 52%.

For the full year 2026, the company now expects total net sales to be between €36B and €40B (midpoint at €38B), compared to the [prior](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4543340-asml-rises-as-record-orders-beat-estimates-amid-ai-related-demand?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "prior") forecast of €34B to €39B (midpoint at €36.5B) provided in January with the fourth quarter results. ASML expects full-year gross margin between 51% and 53%.

## SA Analyst Commentary

ASML’s Q1 sales showed sales that were near the high end of the guided €8.2-€8.8 billion range with gross margins meeting the high end of the range. More interesting was that the company increased its revenue guidance from €34-€39 billion to €36-€40 billion for 2026. That is a strong sign as it confirms the robustness of demand, but also that even with a tight supply chain ASML has found some space to generate €1-€2 billion higher sales this year than initially targeted and that includes export control headwinds. So, that likely also points at some improvement in ASML’s own supply chain, which I believe is a positive forward indicator for future years as well," said Seeking Alpha analyst [Dhierin Bechai](https://seekingalpha.com/author/dhierin-bechai?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "Dhierin Bechai"), Investing Group Leader for The Aerospace Forum.

Bechai added that "demand remains robust and ASML is now showing that it can deliver more than it initially expected. While that is a positive, we note that analysts were already expecting revenues near the mid-point of the new range. The new guidance supports that."

## Wall Street Analysts

JPMorgan analyst Sandeep Deshpande noted that ASML raising guidance at the first quarter rather than half-year shows the company’s confidence in demand strength, Bloomberg reported. ASML’s positive outlook with indications of “very strong” orders reads positively for other chip equipment companies, the analyst added.

Lee Simpson, analyst at Morgan Stanley, said that despite no mention of bookings, the company talked of demand outstripping supply and customers looking to accelerate capacity expansion, which suggests strong sales momentum into 2027. Simpson added that the guidance for at least 80 low-NA EUV tools available next year is positive, and that number could still rise on any determined buildout of clean room space available.

Analysts at Berenberg said that the guidance raise is “kind of” expected by the Street, although that signals the company’s confidence given it’s just the first quarter. Focus is mainly on 2027 at this point, and end-market commentary from the company continues to be solid, the analysts added.

"ASML provided a decent beat in its latest results, but nothing exceptional for what is a high-quality company with an enviable market position," said Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot. The analyst noted that the guidance raise "brings it more in line with where the market expects it to be, but a positive move nonetheless."

## Dividend and Buyback

ASML said it intends to declare a total dividend for the year 2025 of €7.50 per ordinary share, which is a 17% increase compared to 2024. Recognizing the three interim dividends of €1.60 per ordinary share paid in 2025 and 2026, this leads to a final dividend proposal to the Annual General Meeting of €2.70 per ordinary share.

ASML noted that in the first quarter, it bought back about €1.1B worth of shares under the 2026–2028 share buyback program. The company intends to buy back shares worth up to €12B under this program.

Shares of other chip equipment makers on Wednesday. KLA ( [KLAC](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KLAC?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "KLA Corporation")) slumped about 4%, while Lam Research ( [LRCX](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/LRCX?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "Lam Research Corporation")) fell around 3%. Applied Materials ( [AMAT](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMAT?utm_source=msn.com&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news&fr=1 "Applied Materials, Inc.")) dipped about 2% on Wednesday.

# Pressure on ASML share price due to postponement of TSMC order

TSMC postpones ASML’s extremely expensive high-NA EUV machines until 2029. What does this mean for the chip sector?

Published on April 27, 2026

![ASML Campus Veldhoven](https://ioplus.nl/_next/image?url=%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2FASML_Aerial_Campus_Veldhoven_Aug2021_0052.jpg&w=2048&q=75)

ASML Campus Veldhoven

[![Team IO+  ](https://ioplus.nl/_next/image?url=%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2FIO%252B%2520logo%2520kruis.jpeg&w=2048&q=75)](https://ioplus.nl/en/authors/team-io)[**By: Team IO+**](https://ioplus.nl/en/authors/team-io)

Team IO+ selects and features the most important news stories on innovation and technology, carefully curated by our editors.

[Share on BlueSky](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Check%20out%20this%20article:%20https://ioplus.nl/en/posts/pressure-on-asml-share-price-due-to-postponement-of-tsmc-order)[Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://ioplus.nl/en/posts/pressure-on-asml-share-price-due-to-postponement-of-tsmc-order)[Share on Mastodon](https://mastodon.social/share?text=Check%20out%20this%20article:%20https://ioplus.nl/en/posts/pressure-on-asml-share-price-due-to-postponement-of-tsmc-order)[Share on Threads](https://www.threads.net/intent/post?text=Check%20out%20this%20article:%20https://ioplus.nl/en/posts/pressure-on-asml-share-price-due-to-postponement-of-tsmc-order)[Share on WhatsApp](https://wa.me/?text=Check%20out%20this%20article:%20https://ioplus.nl/en/posts/pressure-on-asml-share-price-due-to-postponement-of-tsmc-order)

On April 23, the chip sector woke up to a sharp price drop at ASML. The share of the Veldhoven giant fell by 3.3 percent in a single day. The direct reason was an announcement by TSMC, one of the company’s most important customers. The Taiwanese chip manufacturer has decided to postpone adopting the latest generation of lithography machines.

This concerns the so-called high-NA EUV systems, which are considered essential for the next generation of superchips. TSMC is now choosing to deploy this technology on a large scale only around 2029. This decision exposes the tension between technological ambition and economic feasibility in the global semiconductor industry.

## The sky-high price of innovation

The core of the problem is simply the price of the new hardware. A single high-NA EUV machine from ASML currently costs more than 350 million euros. Converted, that is more than 410 million dollars per device. Kevin Zhang, an important executive at TSMC, indicated that the machines are currently too expensive for profitable mass production. TSMC is critically examining the cost per chip produced. The current generation of EUV machines is already costly, but the switch to high-NA requires an even larger investment.

![Wayne Allan, Roger Dassen, ASML board](https://ioplus.nl/_next/image?url=%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2FWayne%2520Allan%252C%2520Roger%2520Dassen%252C%2520ASML%2520board&w=828&q=75)

#### Brainport’s next test: diversify at home, scale in Asia

At the EY BrainportConnect event in Eindhoven, ASML’s Roger Dassen and Wayne Allan show what's needed to stay competitive.

[Read More](https://ioplus.nl/en/posts/brainports-next-test-diversify-at-home-scale-in-asia)

For ASML, this means that the expected billions in revenue from these new systems will arrive later than planned. The company from Veldhoven had hoped that the industry would switch more quickly to the new standard. Economic reality, however, forces TSMC to pause. They first want to extract maximum value from their existing machine park before investing billions again. This postponement creates uncertainty among investors who had counted on a faster growth spurt in revenue.

## Smart alternatives for the short term

Meanwhile, TSMC is not standing still and has developed technological alternatives. They state that they can still manage for the coming years without the new high-NA machines. For their so-called A14 node, which operates at 1.4 nanometers, they rely on process optimizations. TSMC uses advanced nanosheet architectures for their transistors. According to the company, this technique offers up to 15 percent higher performance or 30 percent lower energy consumption. They achieve this result without purchasing the newest machines.

In addition, TSMC is experimenting with advanced packaging techniques such as CoWoS and 3D-IC to increase chip density. Through these smart innovations, they can postpone the necessity of the very latest lithography for a while longer. For the European chip sector, this is a relevant signal. It shows that process innovation is not always dependent on the newest hardware. Still, the question remains how long TSMC can maintain this strategy before the physical limits of the current machines are reached. For now, however, the focus seems to be entirely on maximizing the current EUV fleet.

![BvOF-2018_0117_AJY-ASML-logo.jpg](https://ioplus.nl/_next/image?url=%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2FBvOF-2018_0117_AJY-ASML-logo-2.jpg&w=828&q=75)

#### ASML raises expectations due to AI boom

ASML posts strong results in Q1 2026 and raises its annual outlook thanks to the enormous demand for AI chips.

[Read More](https://ioplus.nl/en/posts/asml-raises-expectations-due-to-ai-boom)

## Competitors choose a different path

Remarkably, TSMC’s competitors are following a very different course. While the Taiwanese are waiting, parties such as Intel and Samsung are fully committing to high-NA EUV. Intel has already put the Twinscan EXE:5200B machine into use for the development of its 14A process. They want to use this to recapture their lost technological lead over TSMC. Samsung has also not stood still and received its first high-NA machine at the end of 2025. They are planning a second machine for the first half of 2026 to strengthen their 2nm production lines. Even SK Hynix had already installed such a system in September 2025 for the production of advanced memory.

This creates an interesting dynamic in the market. TSMC is betting on efficiency and cost control, while the competition is betting on early adoption of the latest technology. If Intel’s strategy succeeds, this could shift the balance of power in the chip world. For ASML, this spreading of risk is good news. Although its largest customer is slowing down, other giants continue investing in the future of lithography.

## Impact on ASML’s long-term vision

The postponement by TSMC has direct consequences for ASML’s financial targets. The company is aiming for annual revenue of 60 billion euros in 2030. Analysts see the current postponement as a temporary setback, also called a “timing headwind.” It does not mean demand is disappearing, but that the peak in revenue is moving backward. ASML must now adapt its strategy to bridge this period. The focus will likely shift more toward sales of the current generation of EUV systems and their maintenance.

ASML must also continue its R&D efforts to increase the productivity of the high-NA machines. If the machines can produce more chips per hour, the price of 350 million euros becomes easier to justify for TSMC. Pressure on the engineers in Veldhoven is therefore increasing. They must prove that the new technology is not only technically superior, but also economically profitable. The market is now looking critically at the results of the coming quarters to see whether other customers follow TSMC’s example.

## The role of the AI revolution

Despite the delay at TSMC, overall demand for chips remains unprecedentedly high. This is mainly due to the continuing boom in artificial intelligence (AI). AI chips require the most powerful hardware, which keeps demand for ASML’s current EUV machines robust. Suppliers in the lithography chain are therefore reacting cautiously to the news from Taiwan. They do see slower growth for specific high-NA components, but the underlying demand remains stable. For European strategic autonomy, this is an important point. ASML remains the only supplier in the world of these crucial machines. Whether TSMC buys them in 2026 or 2029, they cannot avoid Dutch technology. The postponement also gives European industry a little more time to optimize the supply chains for these complex systems. The semiconductor market is always cyclical and subject to political and economic shifts. The current postponement is a reminder that even the most advanced technology must bend to the laws of economics.

By

[Transcripts](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts)

Published 04/24/2026, 06:46 AM

Earnings call transcript: ASML beats Q1 2026 earnings forecast, stock dips

[View all comments (0)0](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-asml-beats-q1-2026-earnings-forecast-stock-dips-93CH-4635181#comments-4635181)

ASML Holding NV reported robust financial results for the first quarter of 2026, with earnings per share (EPS) of EUR 7.15, surpassing the forecast of EUR 7.7. The company achieved a revenue of EUR 8.8 billion, exceeding expectations and highlighting strong demand for its semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Despite this performance, ASML’s stock fell by 7.08% in pre-market trading, reflecting potential investor concerns over future margin trends.

## **Key Takeaways**

- ASML’s EPS of EUR 7.15 exceeded forecasts, with a revenue surprise of 16.97%.
- Stock price declined by 7.08% in pre-market trading despite positive earnings.
- Strong demand for semiconductor equipment continues to drive revenue growth.
- Future margin expectations are slightly moderated for Q2 2026.
- Operational challenges and supply chain considerations remain key focus areas.

## **Company Performance**

ASML delivered a strong performance in Q1 2026, driven by unprecedented demand for its advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The company’s revenue and EPS both exceeded forecasts, reflecting a continuation of its growth trajectory. ASML’s strategic focus on EUV and High-NA platforms has positioned it well in the competitive landscape, despite sector-wide supply chain challenges.

## **Financial Highlights**

- Revenue: EUR 8.8 billion, surpassing forecasts and previous guidance.
- Earnings per share: EUR 7.15, above the forecasted EUR 7.7.
- Gross margin: 53%, at the high end of guidance.
- Net income: EUR 2.8 billion, representing 31.4% of total net sales.

## **Earnings vs. Forecast**

ASML’s Q1 2026 earnings per share of EUR 7.15 exceeded the forecast of EUR 7.7, marking a surprise of 7.27%. The company’s revenue of EUR 8.8 billion also surpassed the expected EUR 8.66 billion, resulting in a revenue surprise of 16.97%. This performance indicates strong operational execution and robust market demand.

## **Market Reaction**

Despite the positive earnings surprise, ASML’s stock fell by 7.08% in pre-market trading, dropping from EUR 1518.3 to EUR 1410.83. This decline suggests investor concerns over future profitability, particularly regarding margin compression as indicated in the company’s Q2 guidance. The stock, however, remains near its 52-week high, trading just 8% below its peak of $1,547. According to [InvestingPro](https://www.investing.com/pro/ASML) analysis, the stock currently appears overvalued relative to its Fair Value—a concern that may be contributing to the selloff despite strong quarterly results. The company trades at a P/E ratio of 47.6 and a PEG ratio of 2.79, suggesting premium valuations. Investors can explore similar valuation concerns across the market on InvestingPro’s [Most Overvalued stocks list](https://www.investing.com/equities/most-overvalued).

## **Outlook & Guidance**

ASML has provided guidance for Q2 2026, with gross margin expectations of 51-52%, reflecting a more normalized business mix.
